title: Deepwalk: Online Learning of Social Representations
text: Deepwalk learns latent representations of nodes in a graph by treating truncated random walks as sentences and applying techniques inspired by word representation learning. The method is unsupervised and is designed to capture graph neighborhood structure. Deepwalk was evaluated on multi-label node classification tasks and demonstrated that random-walk-based representations can provide useful features for downstream learning.

title: Variational Graph Auto-Encoders
text: Variational Graph Auto-Encoders introduce a probabilistic auto-encoder framework for graph-structured data. The encoder is based on graph convolutional networks and maps nodes to latent variables represented by a mean and variance. The decoder reconstructs graph connectivity using latent node representations. VGAE is mainly evaluated on link prediction using citation-network datasets such as Cora, Citeseer, and Pubmed.

title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
text: Graph Convolutional Networks provide an efficient neural architecture for learning on graph-structured data. The model propagates and transforms information from neighboring nodes using a normalized graph adjacency matrix. GCN was proposed for semi-supervised node classification and was evaluated on citation-network datasets including Cora, Citeseer, and Pubmed. The GCN architecture later became a common encoder for many graph representation learning models, including VGAE.

title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
text: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry presents the message passing neural network framework, which describes many graph neural networks using a common formulation. During message passing, node states are updated using information received from neighboring nodes and edges. A readout function then produces a graph-level representation. The framework was demonstrated on molecular property prediction tasks and helped establish message passing as a general abstraction for graph neural networks.

title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
text: GraphSAGE is an inductive framework for generating node embeddings by sampling and aggregating features from a node's local neighborhood. Unlike transductive embedding methods, GraphSAGE learns aggregation functions that can generate representations for previously unseen nodes. Several neighborhood aggregators were studied, including mean, LSTM, and pooling aggregators. GraphSAGE was evaluated on node classification and representation learning tasks on large graphs.

title: Graph Attention Networks
text: Graph Attention Networks introduce attention mechanisms into graph neural networks. Instead of assigning the same normalized importance to all neighbors, GAT learns attention coefficients that determine how strongly each neighboring node contributes to the representation of a target node. Multi-head attention is used to improve stability and representation capacity. GAT was evaluated on node classification benchmarks including Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, and PPI.

title: How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?
text: This work studies the expressive power of graph neural networks and relates neighborhood aggregation to the Weisfeiler-Lehman graph isomorphism test. The authors propose the Graph Isomorphism Network, or GIN, which uses a sum aggregation function followed by a multilayer perceptron. GIN is designed to distinguish graph structures more effectively than several common aggregation schemes. The model was evaluated primarily on graph classification benchmarks.

title: Simplifying Graph Convolutional Networks
text: Simplifying Graph Convolutional Networks analyzes the nonlinearities and weight matrices used in GCN and proposes Simple Graph Convolution. SGC repeatedly propagates node features over the graph and then applies a linear classifier. The method shows that some graph convolutional models can retain strong node classification performance even after removing intermediate nonlinear transformations. SGC was evaluated on citation and social-network node classification datasets.
